overall: The AG found four meeting-notice violations (Oct 2010–Jan 2011) and noted minutes omissions, but imposed no penalties because the Council had remedied them and voluntarily disclosed them; the non-OML objections were not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complaint singled out the March 3, 2011 meeting as an example of ongoing violations, without identifying specific violations at that meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Nevertheless, our review of this matter revealed violations by the Council at the meeting, such as failure to list topics in meeting notices.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged minutes were not always available to the public, or made available timely upon request and within a reasonable period after meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Upon review, it appears that the Council has generally been in compliance with the Open Meeting Law's minutes requirements.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council's minutes do not always reflect a comprehensive and accurate view of business addressed.
allegations.key_passage: Although these omissions might appear to be inconsequential oversights, they illustrate the Council's failure to consistently adhere to the minimum requirements set forth in G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a).

allegations.summary: Council admitted holding four meetings between Oct 2010 and Jan 2011 without posting complete topic listings in meeting notices.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Council's admitted failure to publish complete meeting notices, including anticipated agendas, in advance of meetings between October 5, 2010 and January 6, 2011, constituted four separate violations of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant raised several other Council operational objections that the complainant conceded did not concern the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We do not address the complaint's allegations that do not implicate the Open Meeting Law.
